nodes.summary: Centred feature vectors (Schölkopf, Smola and Müller, *Nonlinear component analysis as a kernel eigenvalue problem*, Neural Comput. 10 (1998), Appendix B, equation (B.1)): `Φ̃(xᵢ) = Φ(xᵢ) - (1/M) ∑ₘ Φ(xₘ)`.
nodes.title: Centred feature vectors

nodes.summary: Solutions of the Gram-matrix eigenproblem are kernel principal axes (Schölkopf, Smola and Müller, *Nonlinear component analysis as a kernel eigenvalue problem*, Neural Comput. 10 (1998), equation (2.12)). If `M λ α = K α`, then `V = ∑ᵢ αᵢ Φ(xᵢ)` satisfies `C̄ V = λ V`.
nodes.title: Solutions of the Gram-matrix eigenproblem are kernel principal axes

nodes.summary: `C̄ (∑ᵢ αᵢ Φ(xᵢ)) = (1/M) ∑ᵢ (K α)ᵢ Φ(xᵢ)` (Schölkopf, Smola and Müller, *Nonlinear component analysis as a kernel eigenvalue problem*, Neural Comput. 10 (1998), equation (2.9)).
nodes.title: The covariance operator on kernel expansions

nodes.summary: Covariance operator in feature space (Schölkopf, Smola and Müller, *Nonlinear component analysis as a kernel eigenvalue problem*, Neural Comput. 10 (1998), equation (2.5)). For feature vectors `Φ(x₁), …, Φ(x_M)` it is `C̄ V = (1/M) ∑ⱼ ⟪Φ(xⱼ), V⟫ Φ(xⱼ)`.
nodes.title: Covariance operator in feature space

nodes.summary: Every kernel principal axis comes from the Gram-matrix eigenproblem (Schölkopf, Smola and Müller, *Nonlinear component analysis as a kernel eigenvalue problem*, Neural Comput. 10 (1998), Appendix A). If `C̄ V = λ V` with `λ ≠ 0`, then `V = ∑ᵢ αᵢ Φ(xᵢ)` for some `α` with `M λ α = K α`.
nodes.title: Every kernel principal axis comes from the Gram-matrix eigenproblem

nodes.summary: Kernel expansion in feature space (Schölkopf, Smola and Müller, *Nonlinear component analysis as a kernel eigenvalue problem*, Neural Comput. 10 (1998), equation (2.8)): `V = ∑ᵢ αᵢ Φ(xᵢ)`.
nodes.title: Kernel expansion in feature space

nodes.summary: The centred Gram matrix (Schölkopf, Smola and Müller, *Nonlinear component analysis as a kernel eigenvalue problem*, Neural Comput. 10 (1998), Appendix B, equation (B.3)). With `(1_M)ᵢⱼ = 1/M`, the Gram matrix of the centred feature vectors is `K̃ = K - 1_M K - K 1_M + 1_M K 1_M`, computed from the kernel values alone.
nodes.title: The centred Gram matrix

nodes.summary: `gram Φ x` is `Matrix.gram ℝ (fun i => Φ (xᵢ))`, the matrix of inner products of the feature vectors (Schölkopf, Smola and Müller, *Nonlinear component analysis as a kernel eigenvalue problem*, Neural Comput. 10 (1998), equation (2.10)); in particular it is positive semidefinite.
nodes.title: The kernel PCA Gram matrix is Mathlib's Gram matrix

nodes.summary: The kernel PCA eigenvalue equation in coefficient form (Schölkopf, Smola and Müller, *Nonlinear component analysis as a kernel eigenvalue problem*, Neural Comput. 10 (1998), equations (2.9)–(2.11)). For `V = ∑ᵢ αᵢ Φ(xᵢ)`, `λ V = C̄ V` implies `M λ K α = K² α`.
nodes.title: The kernel PCA eigenvalue equation in coefficient form

nodes.summary: Kernel Gram matrix (Schölkopf, Smola and Müller, *Nonlinear component analysis as a kernel eigenvalue problem*, Neural Comput. 10 (1998), equation (2.10)): `K i j = ⟪Φ(xᵢ), Φ(xⱼ)⟫`, the kernel `k(xᵢ, xⱼ)`. It agrees with Mathlib's `Matrix.gram` (bridge).
nodes.title: Kernel Gram matrix

nodes.summary: Kernel PCA projections (Schölkopf, Smola and Müller, *Nonlinear component analysis as a kernel eigenvalue problem*, Neural Comput. 10 (1998), equation (2.15)). The projection of a test point onto `V = ∑ᵢ αᵢ Φ(xᵢ)` is `⟪V, Φ(t)⟫ = ∑ᵢ αᵢ k(xᵢ, t)`, computed from kernel values only.
nodes.title: Kernel PCA projections

nodes.summary: `⟪∑ᵢ αᵢ Φ(xᵢ), W⟫ = ∑ᵢ αᵢ ⟪Φ(xᵢ), W⟫` (Schölkopf, Smola and Müller, *Nonlinear component analysis as a kernel eigenvalue problem*, Neural Comput. 10 (1998), equations (2.9) and (2.14)).
nodes.title: Inner products of a kernel expansion

nodes.summary: `⟪Φ(x_k), ∑ᵢ αᵢ Φ(xᵢ)⟫ = (K α)_k` (Schölkopf, Smola and Müller, *Nonlinear component analysis as a kernel eigenvalue problem*, Neural Comput. 10 (1998), equations (2.9)–(2.10)).
nodes.title: Feature vectors against a kernel expansion

nodes.summary: Eigenvectors with nonzero eigenvalue lie in the span of the data (Schölkopf, Smola and Müller, *Nonlinear component analysis as a kernel eigenvalue problem*, Neural Comput. 10 (1998), Section 2, before equation (2.8)). If `C̄ V = λ V` with `λ ≠ 0`, then `V` lies in the span of `Φ(x₁), …, Φ(x_M)`.
nodes.title: Eigenvectors with nonzero eigenvalue lie in the span of the data

nodes.summary: Normalization of kernel principal axes (Schölkopf, Smola and Müller, *Nonlinear component analysis as a kernel eigenvalue problem*, Neural Comput. 10 (1998), equation (2.14)). If `M λ α = K α`, then `‖∑ᵢ αᵢ Φ(xᵢ)‖² = M λ (α ⬝ α)`; so `V` has unit norm exactly when `M λ (α ⬝ α) = 1`.
nodes.title: Normalization of kernel principal axes

nodes.summary: Squared norm of a kernel expansion (Schölkopf, Smola and Müller, *Nonlinear component analysis as a kernel eigenvalue problem*, Neural Comput. 10 (1998), equation (2.14), first equality): `‖∑ᵢ αᵢ Φ(xᵢ)‖² = α ⬝ K α`.
nodes.title: Squared norm of a kernel expansion

nodes.summary: The kernel PCA Gram matrix is positive semidefinite, as a Gram matrix of feature vectors (Schölkopf, Smola and Müller, *Nonlinear component analysis as a kernel eigenvalue problem*, Neural Comput. 10 (1998), equations (2.10) and (2.12): the eigenvalues `M λ` of `K` are nonnegative).
nodes.title: The kernel PCA Gram matrix is positive semidefinite

nodes.summary: The centred feature vectors are centred (Schölkopf, Smola and Müller, *Nonlinear component analysis as a kernel eigenvalue problem*, Neural Comput. 10 (1998), Appendix B): `∑ᵢ Φ̃(xᵢ) = 0`.
nodes.title: The centred feature vectors are centred

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
